title: Lesson 6: Estimating Multi-Week Engagements: Beyond the 30-45 Minute Task
description: The 30-45 minute task is the unit of execution, not the unit of estimation. This lesson teaches you to size a real multi-week delivery: how to break a large engagement into estimable pieces, why you estimate the critical path and not the total, how to put the constraints and reviews from Lesson 5 into the number, and how to keep an estimate honest when the environment reveals surprises.

questions.question: What number defines the estimate for a multi-week delivery?
options: The sum of all task effort across the plan
The longest chain of dependent work
The average of the three-point ranges
The total number of scoped tasks
questions.explanation: The end date is set by the longest chain of dependent work, because parallel workstreams run at the same time rather than one after another.

questions.question: Where do fixed-duration gates like a security review belong in the estimate?
options: Hidden inside the build task they affect
Left out until the build is complete
On the critical path as their own items
questions.explanation: A gate runs on its owner's calendar and cannot be compressed by effort, so it must appear as a fixed-duration item on the critical path.

questions.question: How should the ongoing operation of an agent be priced?
options: As part of the one-time build total
As a per-run cost only, with no ongoing rate
As a weekly rate kept apart from the build
As a fixed fee paid once at handover
questions.explanation: The build is a one-time total while the ongoing operation recurs weekly, so it is priced as a rate plus a per-run cost.
